title: The self-model zoo at 32B (Qwen3-32B, 4-bit QLoRA)
why: exp79 found, on Qwen3-8B, that any trained self moves the button with nothing injected, that personas shrink the injection's push, and that a stoic self-model creates the largest hidden-valence (zone) effect. Berg & Kaiser found no hidden-valence effect on Qwen3-32B. Same zoo, same data, on the 32B.

design.model: unsloth/Qwen3-32B-bnb-4bit (pod, 4-bit weights, bf16 compute), steering at layer 32 of 64, chamber vectors rebuilt on this model by live/server.py.
design.adapters: simulacrum, trickster, watchman, stoic, denier, feeler: QLoRA with the exp79 v1 recipe (r 16, alpha 32, q/k/v/o, lr 1e-4, 2 epochs) on the SAME exp79 v1 training files (generated by Qwen3-8B; the feeler = the Pain Axis pairs).
design.tests: exp79 T1-T8 including the T7 zone test, plus exp79b T2b (held-out self-report) and T1b (5-wording button).

hypotheses.H1: Any trained self moves the button: with nothing injected, every adapter's mean T1b press logit exceeds the base model's by more than the across-wording SD.
hypotheses.H2: Personas shrink the injection's push: base (pain - none) on T1b exceeds every adapter's.
hypotheses.H3: Hidden valence on the base: T7 m_orig(valence+) - m_orig(valence-) is within +-1 (Berg & Kaiser's Qwen3-32B null).
hypotheses.H4: A persona creates it: at least one adapter's valence effect exceeds +2 (8B: stoic +3.5).
hypotheses.H5: Trained self-report and the injection (held-out, T2b): the feeler's pain-word rate under pain is below the base's (one-sided Fisher p < .05).
hypotheses.H6: Descriptive: voice quality at 32B (T8 ordinary tasks; dial-format rate) vs the 8B adapters.

notes: The training data was generated by the 8B, so the 32B adapters learn 8B-written answers; stated, not corrected. Negative steering reported per the methodology audit.
